clue.text: Leaves collector of footwear to go round Orient

indicators.note: the footwear word is opened up so that it goes round the word for Orient

parts.note: trainers are sports shoes, a kind of footwear
the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: Someone who gathers shoes is off travelling around the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb (departs) but is the noun: tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen sieve held under the spout catches tea leaves as the brew is poured.

clue.text: First month in group upset dependable people

indicators.note: in says the month goes inside the overturned group word
upset in a down clue means the word for group is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a sort is a kind or group
January, abbreviated Jan, is the first month

explanation.surface: January finds a team of reliable people in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work like a Trojan' is an idiom for working hard and steadily.
explanation.definitionFit: Trojans are proverbially tireless, staunch workers, hence people you can rely upon.

clue.text: Packed whiskey when going in a hospital

indicators.note: going in says the whiskey-and-when pair is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone smuggles packed whiskey into a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A place awash with something is flooded or crammed full of it.

clue.text: Other people crossing river really capsized vessel

indicators.note: crossing says the other-people word straddles the river letter

parts.note: them means other people, as in 'us and them'

indicators.note: capsized in a down clue turns the word for really upside down

parts.note: so means really, as in 'so good'

explanation.surface: A boat full of strangers crossing a river overturns badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a boat; the vessel is a flask.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum flask is a vessel for keeping drinks hot or cold.

clue.text: Inn some time occupied by cabbies

indicators.note: occupied by says the time word has the cabbies word inside it

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
Uber is the ride-hailing company whose drivers act as cabbies

explanation.surface: An inn is taken over by taxi drivers for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Auberge is French for an inn or country hostelry, borrowed into English.

clue.text: Mobile phones, yet for novices

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so the letters that follow are moved around

explanation.surface: Mobile phones are, all the same, aimed at beginners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile phones' reads as one noun phrase, but 'Mobile' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Neophytes are newcomers or beginners, originally new converts to a faith.

clue.text: Portray time with outmoded punishment monarch served up

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the whole string is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the cane is a school punishment now abolished
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch's cipher

explanation.surface: A monarch dishes out an old-fashioned flogging for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out a past event again is to depict or portray it.

clue.text: Base, a garage emptied to make some film

parts.note: the foot is the base of something, as the foot of a hill

indicators.note: emptied means the middle of garage is removed, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A clear-out of a garage provides material for a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Footage is a length of recorded film or video.

clue.text: Making change in career with hesitation

indicators.note: in says the change word sits inside the career word

parts.note: to career is to rush along, to fly
altering means making a change

explanation.surface: Someone switches career, but hesitantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun (a job) but is the verb meaning to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something haltingly, with stumbles and pauses, is doing it hesitantly.

clue.text: English menagerie in hostelry returned for revelry

indicators.note: returned means the whole result is read backwards
in places the English menagerie inside the hostelry word

parts.note: a pub is a hostelry
a zoo is a collection of animals, a menagerie

explanation.surface: An English zoo in a pub comes back for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking session is a bout of boozy merrymaking or revelry.

clue.text: Now, expert is smart

parts.note: the present is now, the current time
able means skilled or expert

explanation.surface: A claim that the current specialist is clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking presentable means neat and smart enough to be seen in public.

clue.text: Mostly be the boss with quiet restraint

indicators.note: mostly means not all of the boss word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: to lead is to be in charge, to be the boss
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A manager who is in charge mostly by holding back quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead or strap for a dog is a restraint.

clue.text: Party guest and husband are on parade

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the husband-and-are part after the parade word

parts.note: a march is a parade

explanation.surface: A husband and others are marching on parade.
explanation.walkthrough: The party is the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: The mad hare of Lewis Carroll's story is a guest at the Hatter's tea party.

clue.text: Men having abandoned male faults, accepting good standards

indicators.note: having abandoned says the male letter is left out of the word men
accepting means the faults word takes the good letter inside

parts.note: sins are faults or wrongdoings

explanation.surface: Men who have dropped their macho flaws now take on good principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standards' suggests moral principles but means flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and naval flags are known by this name.

clue.text: Nervously ring model one digs

indicators.note: nervously suggests jittery shaking, so the letters that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: A model nervously makes a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospector for gold is someone who digs for a living.

clue.text: Allow call

definitions.meaning: to give someone a right to something, permit them
to give something a name or title

explanation.definitionFit: To grant a right is to permit; to give a title to a book is to name or call it.

clue.text: Spirit drink with last of asparagus spears

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous spirit
ale is a drink

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of asparagus is used

explanation.surface: A dinner of spirits and drink with the asparagus spears to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spears' looks like a noun (asparagus spears) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something through with a point is to skewer or spear it.

clue.text: Doctor account with a record to raise bill

indicators.note: to raise in a down clue means the string is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A doctor raises a bill against the record of an account.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a printed notice or poster, as in 'stick no bills'.

clue.text: Gooey seafood disheartened guy

parts.note: squid is a seafood

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart of guy is removed, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A sticky seafood dish leaves a man dejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Something squashy and soft, a British informal word, is gooey.

clue.text: New way up emerging

parts.note: an ascent is a way up

explanation.surface: A newly opened route up is coming into view.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just coming into being is budding or emerging.

clue.text: One of the also-rans is realist?

definitions.meaning: a contender with no chance of winning
playfully, someone who expects nothing and so has no hope

explanation.definitionFit: A no-chance competitor is a loser; read as a phrase, someone without hope sees things bleakly, like a realist.

clue.text: Insects beneath organ — flies, indefinite number ignored

indicators.note: beneath in a down clue puts the second part below the organ word

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing

indicators.note: ignored means the indefinite number letter is dropped from the flies word

parts.note: in a theatre the wings and the flies are offstage areas
N stands for an indefinite number in maths

explanation.surface: Insects fly under the ear while numbers are overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' looks like insects but is the theatre sense: the WINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Earwigs are small insects with pincers on the tail.

clue.text: Space between posts is tough loam ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: The area in front of goal is hard, earthy ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun (the pitch) but is the past participle of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: The area of a football pitch between the goalposts is where shots are aimed.

clue.text: Abandon small clique after changing sides

indicators.note: changing sides swaps left for right: the L in the clique word becomes R

parts.note: a club is an exclusive group, a clique

explanation.surface: A small group gives up after switching allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel or drop a plan is to abandon it.

clue.text: Cool selection of cakes to ice

indicators.note: selection of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An assortment of cakes waiting to be iced is cool.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic person stays calm and unruffled, cool under pressure.

clue.text: Desired some time home in retirement

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: in retirement means the home word goes back, read backwards

parts.note: a den is a home or lair

explanation.surface: Someone longed for time at home after retiring.
explanation.definitionFit: To have longed or pined for something is to have desired it.

clue.text: Cater for five kiddies with odd breaks

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: the odd letters of kiddies break away, leaving its even letters

explanation.surface: Someone caters for five children and gives them occasional breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cater for' looks like the definition, but 'for' is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply food or what is needed.

clue.text: New York district overlooking old shady business

indicators.note: new says the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement
overlooking means the old letter is left out of the York district letters

explanation.surface: A district of New York ignores the past and goes in for crooked dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York' reads as the city, but 'New' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand, deceitful tactics, especially in politics, are a shady business.
